name: Baby monitor
about: Your voice over an old baby monitor: a hiss that breathes with every word, crackle, and the nursery around you.

name: Cassette tape
about: Your voice on a cassette: tape hiss, wow and flutter, warm saturation, dropouts, a dull head, or a chewed-up tape.

name: CB radio
about: A trucker on the citizens band: crackling static, a whistle on the channel, skip fading and an overdriven mic.

name: Wax cylinder
about: A voice from about 1900 on a wax cylinder: narrow and honky, under a roar of hiss, wobbling as the cylinder turns.

name: Gramophone record
about: An old 78 on a wind-up gramophone: horn honk, hissing shellac, crackle, a scratch going round, wobble, and a speed to set.

name: Intercom
about: A voice from a little speaker box: a door buzzer, a drive-through order speaker, an office intercom or a classroom speaker.

name: Megaphone
about: Shouting through a bullhorn: a honking horn, a pushed little amplifier, an optional siren whoop and squeal, and the street echoing back.

name: Answering machine tape
about: A message on an old answering machine: the beep, a phone-line voice on a tiny wobbly tape, hiss and motor whine.

name: PA system
about: An announcement over loudspeakers in a big place: a school gym, an airport, a train station, a stadium or a store.

name: Telephone
about: Your voice down a phone line, from a 1920s candlestick phone to a modern internet call or a speakerphone.

name: AM radio
about: A voice on the AM dial: static, fading and whistles, tuned right in, slightly off, or lost between stations.

name: Police scanner
about: Dispatch chatter on a scanner: squeezed and harsh, with squelch tails, data chirps, or the robotic warble of digital radio.

name: Shortwave
about: A voice from across the world on shortwave: sideband squawk, deep fades, crackling atmosphere and strange signals.

name: Space radio
about: Mission control and the astronauts: a beep tone at the start and end of every transmission, hiss, and the long echo from the moon.

options.name: At the start and the end

name: Tin-can phone
about: Talking through two cans and a string: thin, metallic and ringing, with a springy zing running down the line.

name: Talking toy
about: Your voice coming out of a talking toy: a gritty speech chip, a cheap sample, or a pull-string record, maybe with dying batteries.

name: TV in the next room
about: Your voice on a television somewhere else in the house: through an open door, a closed door, or the wall.

name: Video tape sound
about: The sound of an old home video tape: hiss, wobble, hum and buzz, slower speeds getting duller, and bad tracking bursts.

name: Vinyl record
about: Your voice pressed on a record: dusty crackle, pops, a low rumble, gentle wow, and a warp if you want one.

name: Walkie-talkie
about: A handheld two-way radio: a click as you key up, hiss under your words and a burst of squelch noise when you let go.

name: Canyon calls
about: Shout across a canyon and hear the rock walls answer, each answer further away, fainter and darker.

name: Echo
about: Repeats of your voice, from a quick double to long echoes, centered, bouncing between your ears, or on wobbly old tape.

name: Dub delay
about: A sound-system dub echo: filtered repeats that sweep and swirl, a dripping spring, and feedback that runs away into a swell above 90 percent.

name: Rhythm echoes
about: Several echoes in a rhythm pattern, a gallop, a heartbeat, a bouncing ball, scattered around your head.

name: Reverse reverb swell
about: A ghostly reverb that swells up backwards and rushes into every word, ending just as the word arrives.

name: Reverse echo
about: Every echo is a backwards slice of what you just said, swelling up behind your voice like a tape played in reverse.

name: Slapback
about: One quick slap of an echo right behind your voice, from an old rock and roll tape machine to the far stands of a stadium.

name: 4-bit ADPCM
about: The squeezed sound of old game and answering-machine samples: a hiss that follows your voice and splashy edges on sharp sounds.

name: Blown speaker
about: A wrecked speaker: a torn cone that flaps and rattles, a voice coil that buzzes on loud words, and a loose wire that crackles and cuts out.

name: Phone-line coding
about: The exact digital phone-line sound: 8 kilohertz, 8-bit logarithmic coding, the faint fizz on every word. Fewer bits make a worse line.

name: Old console sound chip
about: Your voice as a sample inside an old game: coded the way each console, handheld, computer or arcade chip really stored and played it.

name: Bit crusher
about: Fewer bits and a lower sample rate: from a slightly grainy voice down to a buzzing, ringing digital wreck.

name: Sample rate reducer
about: Stores the sound at a lower sample rate, like an early sampler: gritty and ringing, or clean and dull like an old voice recorder.

name: Distortion
about: Distorts your voice like a pedal or an amp: warm tube, overdrive, crunch, fuzz, a dying battery, hard clipping, a folder or a rectifier.

name: Old internet file
about: Your voice squeezed into a tiny music file from the dial-up days: swirly and watery, with ghostly pre-echoes before sharp sounds.

name: Tape saturation
about: Warms and thickens your voice like recording it hot onto analogue tape, with the soft squash, the rounded highs and the low head bump.

name: Small speaker
about: Plays your voice through a tiny speaker: an earbud, a phone, a laptop, a toy, a pocket radio, an old TV, a horn or a megaphone.

name: Auto-pan
about: Your voice travels from ear to ear and back, smoothly, in jumps, or wandering around your head.

name: Envelope filter
about: A wah that opens and closes by itself as you speak louder and softer, the funky talking filter sound.

name: Chopper
about: Talking through spinning helicopter blades, or into a fan: the buzzing, chopped, robot-like voice.

name: Chorus
about: Extra copies of your voice drift gently around it, for a thick, shimmering, doubled sound.

name: Pass-by pitch
about: Your voice zooms past like a passing car, train or jet: higher as it comes, lower as it goes.

name: Flanger
about: A sweeping whoosh like a jet plane passing overhead, from gentle swirl to metallic whistle.

name: Rhythm gate
about: Chops your voice on and off in a beat, from a trance gate to a heartbeat or dots and dashes.

name: Keyed by your voice
about: Another sound that plays only while you talk, dips under you, or swells with you: your own sound, rain, a crowd and more.

name: Phaser
about: A soft, liquid swirl that sweeps through your voice, from gentle shimmer to bubbling space sounds.

name: Rotating speaker
about: Your voice through a spinning organ speaker cabinet: swirling horn and drum, slow or fast, with the speed-up ramp.

name: Tremolo
about: Your voice pulses louder and softer, from a gentle shimmer to a hard machine-gun stutter.

name: Underwater
about: Your voice with your head under water: muffled, wavering and bubbling every time you speak.

name: Melody voice
about: Sings your speech along a stepping melody: your words, but on the notes of a chord or scale.

options.name: Back to the key note between notes

params.name: Start each phrase on the key note

name: Pitch correction
about: Snaps your voice onto the notes of a key. Retune speed 0 is the hard robotic snap; 50 to 100 milliseconds sounds natural.

name: Monotone
about: Flattens the melody out of your voice, from a bored drone to a dead-flat robot on one note.

name: Rising or falling
about: Your voice slides from one pitch to another across the whole clip, rising or sinking as you talk.

name: Harmony in a key
about: Adds one or two harmony singers who stay in the key of the song: a third above in C major is sometimes four semitones and sometimes three, as a real singer would do it.

options.name: The same note, a second singer
The same note, a second singer

params.name: Snap the harmony to the notes

name: Harmony voices
about: Extra singers made from your voice join in on a chord, each with its own timing, tuning and timbre.

name: Gas voices
about: The squeaky helium-balloon voice, or the deep heavy-gas voice: the gas moves your timbre, not your note.

name: Cracking voice
about: Your voice cracks, trembles and shakes: a breaking teenage voice, nerves, fear or old age.

name: Octave stack
about: Adds your voice an octave or two below and an octave above: monk chant, giant chorus.

name: Tape speed
about: Plays your voice faster or slower like a tape, so pitch and speed change together.

name: Growl and fry
about: Adds a growling undertone, gravel and creak to your voice: demons, zombies, monsters.

name: Tempo without pitch
about: Talks faster or slower while your voice keeps its own pitch.

name: Vibrato
about: Makes your voice waver up and down like a singer holding a note.

name: Pitch and timbre
about: Moves your voice up or down. Timbre makes the person sound bigger or smaller, without changing the note.

options.name: Smooth, best for music and sounds

name: Warble and drift
about: Your pitch wanders and wobbles: drunk, seasick, nervous or a warped tape.

name: Far away
about: Your voice from far off: across a field, down the street, or the far end of a huge hall.

name: Gated reverb
about: The huge 1980s drum-room sound on your voice: a big burst of room behind each word that stops dead.

name: Hall reverb
about: A concert hall around your voice: a short gap, wide early echoes, then a long warm tail. The classic reverb for a slow song.

name: Through a wall
about: Your voice from the next room: through a door, a wall, the floor upstairs, a car window or a heating vent.

name: Plate reverb
about: The bright, smooth studio reverb from a ringing steel plate: dense from the first instant, with no echoes in it. A classic on singing.

name: Reverb
about: A smooth studio reverb you shape yourself: how big, how long, how dark, and how much.

name: Room
about: Puts your voice inside a real place, from a closet or a tin can to a cathedral or a canyon.

name: Shimmer
about: A heavenly reverb whose tail rises an octave or a fifth, like a choir answering from above.

name: Spring tank
about: The twangy, drippy spring reverb of old amps and surf radio: every word bounces down the springs.

name: Half you, half it
about: Melts your voice and another sound into one, from a hint of it to almost all of it.

name: Spectral smear
about: Smears your voice into a lingering dreamy haze, like a ghost echoing itself.

name: Bad internet audio
about: Your voice squeezed through a weak video call: swirly, thin and wobbling underwater.

name: Harmonic comb
about: Tunes your voice to a chord, from a metallic ring to a choir singing your words.

name: Crystallize
about: Keeps only the brightest notes inside your voice and lets them ring like glass and ice.

name: Glitchy call
about: Bits of your voice drop out like a bad call, hidden by stutters, robot buzz or silence.

name: Spectral freeze
about: Catches moments of your voice and holds them ringing, like a sound frozen in ice.

name: Mirror spectrum
about: Flips your voice inside out, lows become highs, like an old scrambled radio.

name: Words made of sound
about: Your words spoken by the wind, rain, fire, the sea, an organ, bells or any sound you give it.

name: Extreme stretch
about: Stretches your voice many times longer into a slow, shimmering ambient cloud.

name: Robotizer
about: Turns your voice into a steady robot buzz that still says every word.

name: Spectral shift
about: Slides every frequency of your voice by the same amount, so it turns metallic and alien.

name: Spectral stretch
about: Pulls the harmonics of your voice apart or squeezes them together, for bell and metal voices.

name: Spectral gate
about: Keeps only the strongest notes of your voice for a skeleton sound, or only the breath for a wispy ghost.

name: Whisperizer
about: Takes the pitch out of your voice so every word comes out as a breathy whisper.

name: Crowd of you
about: A whole crowd made of you: every person a different pitch, size, timing and place, from a small group to a choir or an army.

name: Double-track
about: Your voice recorded again and again, each take a little early or late and a little off pitch, spread wide.

name: Fly-by
about: Your voice zooms past you from one side to the other, its pitch dropping as it goes by, like a passing car or jet.

name: Short-delay widen
about: One ear hears your voice a few milliseconds late, so it sounds wide and leans toward the other side.

name: Circling head
about: Your voice circles around your head on headphones, past each ear and behind you, and can swoop over the top.

name: Ping-pong phrases
about: Each phrase you say jumps to the other ear, left, right, left. Or every syllable, for a dizzy bounce.

name: Put the voice somewhere
about: Places your voice around your head on headphones: beside you, behind you, above you, in your ear or across the room.

name: Split personality
about: Two different people made from your voice, one in each ear, talking together or taking turns.

name: Walking away or toward
about: The talker walks away from you while speaking, fading into the room, or walks up close from far away.

name: Width
about: Makes the sound wider or narrower. A mono voice is spread into real stereo that still sounds right in mono.

name: Fast flutter
about: Pulses your volume tens or hundreds of times a second: a gargle, a voice through a fan, or the buzz of insect wings.

name: Voice inside a sound
about: Your voice poured into another sound: it rings through bells, a gong or glasses, rumbles in thunder, patters in rain, or takes on any sound you give it.

name: Frequency wobble
about: Wobbles the pitch of your voice fast or slow: a seasick warble, a watery alien, or a buzzing voice at high speeds.

name: Vowel filter
about: Lays moving vowels over your voice: a talking wah, a mouth harp boing, or a vowel that opens as you get louder.

name: Frequency shifter
about: Slides every part of your voice up or down by the same number of hertz: a radio tuned slightly off, or an uneasy alien.

name: Grain cloud
about: Breaks your voice into tiny grains and scatters them: a shimmer, a swarm of you, or a memory falling apart.

name: Kazoo
about: Your voice through a buzzing kazoo, a comb and paper, or a giant kazoo. Hum, sing or talk into it.

name: Speech chip
about: Your voice rebuilt by an old speech chip: a talking learning toy, an arcade game announcer, or a 2400 bit-per-second secure military phone.

name: Resonator bank
about: Your voice rings a real object: a church bell, a wine glass, a gong, a singing bowl, chimes, a steel drum or strings.

name: Ring modulator
about: Multiplies your voice by a tone, so it rings like metal: the tin-voiced space invader, or a clanging robot when set high.

name: Sympathetic strings
about: Six tuned strings ring along with your voice, and every word plucks the chord: a harp, a piano with the pedal down, or a buzzing sitar.

name: Talk box
about: A real talk box: a funk synth, fuzz guitar, organ or any other sound is shaped by your mouth, so the instrument says your words.

name: Vocoder
about: The classic robot choir: your words played by a synth chord, an organ, a choir pad, the wind, or any other sound.

name: Slow-motion stretch
about: Draws your voice out slower, keeping your pitch for a lazy drawl, or dropping it like a slow-motion film shot.

params.name: Stretch the vowels most, when keeping pitch

name: Glitch
about: Breaks your voice into beat-repeat glitches: slices that repeat on a tempo, flip backwards, jump in pitch and roll faster.

name: There and back
about: Plays forward and then straight back again, for the whole clip, each phrase or each word.

name: Backwards
about: Plays the whole clip backwards, last sound first. Add some of the forward voice underneath for a haunted message.

name: Backwards words
about: Every syllable or word plays backwards in its own place, so your sentence keeps its rhythm but turns into a secret language.

name: Record scratch
about: A DJ scratches the first word of each phrase in time before letting it play, or spins the record backwards.

name: Scrambled order
about: Your words come out in a jumbled order, like a message cut up and pasted back together wrong.

name: Stutter
about: Fires off the start of a word again and again before the word goes on, like a stutter edit in a dance track.

name: Tape stop
about: Your voice slows down to a dead stop, like a turntable losing power, and can start up again from standstill.

name: Close the gaps
about: Cuts long pauses down to a short breath, so you sound like a fast talker or a tight radio edit.

params.name: Trim the start and end too

name: Broadcast processor
about: The loud, close, on-air radio sound: steady level riding, four-band compression, presence and a peak limiter, from a light polish to full squeeze.

name: Character
about: Instant voice colours in one choice: radio voice, warm and close, bright and airy, nasal, boomy, telephone, muffled and more.

name: Compressor
about: Evens out your voice: loud words are turned down, quiet ones come up, for a closer, steadier sound. Mix blends in the untouched voice.

name: Click and pop removal
about: Finds mouth clicks, lip smacks and record ticks and fills each one in from the sound around it, leaving your words untouched.

name: De-esser
about: Tames harsh s and sh sounds without a lisp: only the hiss band is turned down, only on s sounds, and never all the way.

name: Hum removal
about: Removes mains hum and buzz at 50 or 60 hertz and their harmonics with narrow notches that leave your voice alone.

name: Noise reduction
about: Removes steady hiss, hum and room noise. It learns the noise from your own pauses and smooths the result so nothing warbles.

name: Equalizer
about: Six bands of boost and cut, each a bell, shelf, cut or notch. Starts on a gentle voice polish; set the gains to 0 for flat.

name: Filter
about: A resonant filter: low pass, high pass, band pass or notch. Leave it still, or let it sweep slowly, drift, or open as you talk.

name: Volume
about: Turns the voice up or down, and can flip its polarity.

name: Noise gate
about: Quiets the pauses between your words so hiss and room noise drop away, and opens a moment before each word so nothing is clipped.

name: Limiter
about: Stops the loudest moments at a ceiling so nothing clips. Push the sound into it to make everything louder and denser.

name: Loudness
about: Sets the whole take to a loudness target, like minus 16 for podcasts, and keeps the peaks under a ceiling.

name: Mono and swap
about: Folds a stereo take to mono, keeps only the left or right side, or swaps the two sides.

name: Tilt
about: One knob from darker to brighter: the top and bottom of your voice see-saw around a middle point, and the overall volume stays put.
